key_insight: Scale weight decay by the current learning rate fraction so regularization fades with training, preserving the optimizer’s asymptotic target while avoiding the steady shrinkage caused by constant decoupled weight decay.
engineering_relevance: This is a low-code training change that can improve large-scale model pretraining efficiency and stability, especially for mixture-of-experts and other long-run setups.
method: Replace constant decoupled weight decay with a schedule proportional to η/η_max.
Analyze the update under Robbins–Monro conditions to retain asymptotic stationarity for SGD and Muon.
Use steady-state analysis to explain why weight norms stabilize instead of continually shrinking.
evidence_signal: On mixture-of-experts models from 72M to 930M parameters, Muon with scaled weight decay reached the same validation loss 30% faster at the largest scale.
watch_item: The reported speedup is from a specific MoE training regime, so benefits may vary with optimizer choice, data scale, and learning-rate scheduling details.
paper_title: Scale Weight Decay and Train Better
